what: ADAPTATIONS OF TOLKIEN'S WORK -- films, television, radio, video games, tabletop games, music and print -- and where named adaptations DIVERGE from the text. A SEPARATE LAYER, in a separate file, because the protocol asks for separately queryable layers and a flag inside the canon datasets fails its own audit 4 by construction.
no_tier: NO ROW CARRIES A TIER. The tiers rank claims about ARDA by distance from Tolkien's word; an adaptation makes a claim about a FILM. Every row carries a HAND, a SOURCE URL, a RETRIEVED_AT and a LICENCE AS STATED instead. Note also C474: `tier: 5` elsewhere in this archive is an ORIGIN axis meaning made by this archive, with `content_tier` beside it -- a different axis again, and nothing here carries either.
why_corpus_tier_and_not_tier: A locus carries `corpus_tier` -- the tier of the CORPUS FILE a quotation was found in, which is a property of the shelf and not a rank on this row. It is named `corpus_tier` rather than `tier` so that a reader grepping this file for a tier finds nothing that could be mistaken for one.
not_the_canon: Nothing in this file is evidence about Middle-earth. A reader who wants what Tolkien wrote wants site/arda_quotes.json or the corpus; a reader who wants what a fan believes wants site/arda_fanon.json.
sibling: site/arda_fanon.json holds the fan layer. The two are separate files for the same reason both are separate from the canon datasets.
publication_layer_what: §IV's `publication_layer` -- the SAME key C490 ruled carries §IV's claim-status vocabulary, not a second field beside it -- on the `adaptation_side` of every deviation. THIS IS THE ONLY THING IN THE ARCHIVE THAT MAKES A CLAIM QUERYABLE AS ADAPTATION-ONLY. A reader asks it with `.deviations[] | select(.adaptation_side.publication_layer)`, or across the whole published set by the value, which is how the 5,004 FANON lexicon records are already found. Its nineteen values are frozen in research/registry/schema/source.schema.json and guarded by map/publayer_check.py; every stamp carries a `publication_layer_basis` naming what it was read from, because a classification nobody can overrule is not published.
publication_layer_not_on_works: A `works` row records that an adaptation EXISTS; §IV's `publication_layer` classifies a CLAIM's standing (C490). It is left off deliberately and not for want of trying: five of the 76 works are fan films and two of the print rows are a parody and an unauthorised retelling, and nothing in the Wikidata harvest held here separates them from the licensed productions, so a medium-to-layer map would publish a false ADAPTATION or a false LICENSED_DERIVATIVE_WORK on seven rows. The DEVIATIONS carry the field instead, because each of those is a claim about one named work.
publication_layer_not_on_the_text_side: The `text_side` of a deviation is Tolkien's own sentence and carries NO layer. Its honest value is TOLKIEN_PRIMARY_PUBLISHED or TOLKIEN_PRIMARY_POSTHUMOUS depending on which VOLUME each locus falls in -- C490's other axis, `first_publication`, which no row here carries. Guessing between the two would put a false stamp on Tolkien's own words to fill a column.

refusals.authority: C477, the owner's ruling of 26 August 2026: his authorisation OVERRIDES the site's reservation for this archive. The same ruling records the session's own limit, which is kept here: this archive will not spoof a User-Agent to evade a block that names it, because misrepresenting what we are is the one thing this archive's ethic forbids absolutely.
refusals.what_was_done: The override was EXERCISED rather than declined. Identifying honestly as a Claude agent acting for this archive, https://www.mobygames.com/game/the-hobbit/ was requested once on 2026-08-26T21:56:30Z. The host returned HTTP 403 and a 55-byte body reading that one should contact the site owner for access. The body was SNIFFED rather than trusted to the status line, and is held in the stage. No page was taken, and no second attempt was made under a different name.
refusals.substitute: Wikidata, CC0, supplied the MobyGames identifiers on the work rows without touching the refusing host.

refusals.authority: This archive's own standing rule that could-not-ask is never a measurement. refusals.authority: Read as a directive to CRAWLERS about indexable paths rather than a bar on the query service itself, which exists to be queried programmatically.
